scope.endpoint: Progression-free survival: time from randomization to RECIST 1.1 progression or death
scope.timepoint: One-year survival estimate; HR across follow-up, median 27.7 months among survivors
scope.population: 167 eligible participants without diabetes with unresectable stage III NSCLC, Zubrod performance status 0–1
scope.comparison: Oral metformin escalated to 2,000 mg/day during concurrent chemoradiotherapy and consolidation chemotherapy versus the same cancer treatment alone
scope.formulation: Release formulation not established in the bounded material inspected

records.finding: Metformin did not demonstrate a progression-free-survival improvement.
records.rationale: Central randomized allocation and blinded imaging re-review support an informative comparison. The wide interval, open treatment allocation and limited metformin adherence leave substantial uncertainty about the treatment effect.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Central stratified randomization; 167/170 eligible participants analyzed by assignment. Open-label treatment, with blinded central progression review supporting the institutional analysis. Only 39% maintained the indicated dose without modification.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: Directly addresses this chemoradiation/consolidation regimen in nondiabetic stage III disease; it does not establish effects with contemporary consolidation immunotherapy or in diabetes.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The PFS interval permits benefit and substantial harm; a nonsignificant result is not equivalence. One-year rates and the follow-up-wide HR have different time interpretations.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: This is one trial. The separate ALMERA trial does not show benefit either but reported worse outcomes; those divergent magnitudes should not be represented as replication of a null effect.

domains.name: Source integrity
domains.text: Received primary full-text HTML methods, Table 2 and limitations inspected. No endpoint-specific correction identified in this bounded material; supplements and a complete version audit remain uninspected.

scope.endpoint: Primary composite of hypoxemia (home oxygen saturation ≤93%), emergency-department visit, hospitalization or death
scope.population: Nonhospitalized adults aged 30–85 with overweight or obesity, infection confirmed within 3 days and symptoms beginning within 7 days; 1,323 in the modified intention-to-treat population
scope.comparison: Immediate-release oral metformin titrated over 6 days to 1,500 mg/day for 14 days versus concurrently randomized control, adjusting for vaccination and the other randomized trial drugs

records.finding: Metformin did not demonstrate a reduction in the primary acute COVID-19 composite outcome.
records.rationale: The masked randomized comparison directly measures the specified acute composite, but unreliable home-oximetry ascertainment and an interval allowing benefit leave material uncertainty. It does not establish equivalence or determine the effect on later Long COVID.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Double-blind factorial randomization with concurrent controls. Prespecified modified intention-to-treat excluded confirmed nonrecipients; primary missing data were imputed. Home oximetry was susceptible to measurement error and undocumented recall.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: Direct early outpatient treatment in adults with overweight/obesity; limited transfer to hospitalized people, normal-weight adults or later variant/vaccination settings. This is not treatment of established Long COVID.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: The adjusted odds interval includes no difference and meaningful benefit. Component outcomes have fewer events and were secondary; their intervals were not adjusted for multiplicity.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: One COVID-OUT trial family. Its Long COVID and viral-RNA reports are other outcomes in overlapping participants, not independent replication of this composite.

domains.name: Source integrity
domains.text: The already-received primary report was checked at methods, primary results and Table 2. The known correction concern attached to the separate Long COVID publication was not assumed to affect this acute report. No complete integrity clearance is claimed.

scope.endpoint: Percentage change in total lean body mass measured by DXA
scope.timepoint: Baseline to study week 16: 14 weeks of supervised progressive resistance training after a 2-week drug wash-in
scope.population: Healthy, predominantly high-functioning older adults, eligibility age 65 years or older; 109 randomized and 94 completers analyzed
scope.comparison: Oral metformin titrated to 1,700 mg/day versus placebo, both with supervised progressive resistance training
scope.formulation: Release formulation not established in the bounded material inspected

records.finding: Total lean-body-mass gains during resistance training were smaller with metformin.
records.magnitudeText: Mean change 0.41% (SD 2.25) with metformin versus 1.95% (SD 2.69) with placebo; between-group P=.003.
records.rationale: The masked randomized comparison directly supports reduced DXA lean-mass gain in this training setting. Completer-only analysis, modest sample size, baseline sex/mass imbalance and absence of a reported effect interval limit confidence and generalization.

domains.name: Study methods
domains.text: Randomized double-blind placebo comparison, but analyses used 94 completers from 109 randomized. Sex distribution generated baseline mass/strength differences; investigators compared percentage changes. No assumption of negligible attrition bias.

domains.name: Directness
domains.text: Directly tests adaptation to supervised training in healthy older people. DXA lean mass is distinct from strength, physical function, walking speed, sarcopenia treatment and longevity.

domains.name: Precision
domains.text: Between-group P=.003 supports a difference; reported arm means and SDs do not supply an effect confidence interval. No interval or graph-derived effect was calculated.

domains.name: Consistency
domains.text: One trial. DXA thigh mass and CT measures are related outcomes in overlapping participants, not independent replication; the strength outcomes are separate.

domains.name: Source integrity
domains.text: Original full XML and actual correction notice DOI 10.1111/acel.13098 inspected. The correction identifies relative strength in Table 2 and related Appendix S2 measures; it does not identify the DXA total-lean-mass result as corrected. Original relative-strength numbers must not be reused. Updated Appendix S2 remains unavailable, so this is endpoint-bounded reconciliation, not completion of the paper review.

basis.locator: DOI 10.1111/acel.13039: Results §§2.1–2.2, Figure 2b caption; Methods §§4.4 and 4.8. Correction DOI 10.1111/acel.13098: opening paragraph and corrected Table 2.

missingness: Updated Appendix S2 and remaining supplement/protocol detail uninspected.
The corrected relative-strength result remains nonsignificant (P=.30), but it is excluded from this lean-mass grade.
Full-paper correction reconciliation remains unfinished; no currently identified correction changes this narrowly assessed DXA endpoint.

limitations: Updated Appendix S2 and remaining supplement/protocol detail uninspected.
